reasons.reproducibility: Review; the typical application study is a sterile lab co-culture needing purchased algicidal strains and microbiology gear.
reasons.effectiveness: Evidence is almost all lab culture; the only field trials (P. fluorescens SK09 in river enclosures) gave inconsistent results.
reasons.cost: Typical lab co-culture needs purchased bacterial and algal strains plus media, roughly $150-500.
reasons.time: Lab algicidal effects in the summarized studies typically show over one to three weeks of co-culture.
reasons.environment: Authors say 'environmentally neutral' claims are untested and live-bacteria dispersal raises biosafety concerns.

reasons.reproducibility: Review; repeating a typical co-culture needs sterile technique and purchased marine algicidal bacteria and algae.
reasons.effectiveness: Authors call the evidence that bacteria end blooms circumstantial; lysis needed >10^6 bacteria/mL and other bacteria blocked it.
reasons.cost: Typical co-culture needs purchased strains and culture media, about $150-500.
reasons.time: Co-culture lysis in the reviewed work typically takes one to three weeks to appear.
reasons.environment: Algicidy is framed as community-wide regulation, so non-target effects on other algae are uncertain.

reasons.reproducibility: Needs Shewanella IRI-160 plus dinoflagellate cultures and alginate beads; sterile microbiology with a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Bead-immobilized bacteria controlled Karlodinium and P. minimum as well as free bacteria; no percentage given.
reasons.time: Growth assays over days; 12-day retention test.
reasons.environment: Beads retained >99% of bacteria after 12 days and spared Rhodomonas.

reasons.reproducibility: Five ~400 L recirculating systems with live fish under diel hypoxia/pH cycling need animal-use approval.
reasons.effectiveness: No algal endpoint; non-target safety study only.
reasons.time: Exposure length not reported; scored conservatively at weeks.
reasons.environment: No cortisol stress response in two estuarine fish at the algicidal dose.

reasons.reproducibility: Two 15,000 L floating mesocosms in a saltwater lake with a native algal virus; field-scale and not school-repeatable.
reasons.effectiveness: Cells fell to ~1% vs 20-30% in the untreated control, significant from day 3, but only one treatment and one control mesocosm on an already-declining bloom.
reasons.cost: Floating 15,000 L mesocosms, boat work and virus assays cost well over $5,000.
reasons.time: Treatment differed from control by day 3 (GLM p<.01) and reached ~1% by day 5.
reasons.environment: 0.1 g/L sediment had no measured effect on water chemistry and HcRNAV is host-specific, but shellfish safety rests partly on unpublished tests.

reasons.reproducibility: Observational field time series of a natural bloom in Hiroshima Bay with virus isolation; not school-repeatable.
reasons.effectiveness: No virus was added and there is no control; the crash is only correlated with HaV and a resistant 10^1-10^2 cells/mL population survived.
reasons.cost: Ship sampling, virus isolation and cross-infection assays cost far over $5,000.
reasons.time: The bloom-to-crash sequence played out over the May-July season, i.e. weeks to months.
reasons.environment: Natural virus is host-specific with no added material, though resistance emerges (susceptibility fell 59% to 18%).

reasons.reproducibility: Co-culture of six bacteria with Cochlodinium needs sterile technique and cultures.
reasons.effectiveness: Negative: Cochlodinium resisted all six algicidal bacteria.
reasons.time: Duration not reported; co-culture tests usually take days.

reasons.reproducibility: Phage work with Microcystis cultures in 96-well plates needs a microbiology lab and phage isolate.
reasons.effectiveness: Cultures collapsed in 3 days at MOI 100 and 3-4 days at MOI 1-10, with controls; lab only.
reasons.environment: Lysis releases intracellular microcystins into water; phage self-propagates.

reasons.reproducibility: Review; typical cyanophage infection assays need purchased host strains and phage isolation skills.
reasons.effectiveness: Only lab infection assays exist, with no field or mesocosm trial and extreme strain specificity (e.g. Ma-LMM01 infects one strain).
reasons.cost: Typical lab infection assay needs purchased cyanobacterial strains and culture supplies, about $150-500.
reasons.time: Lab phage lysis assays typically show results over one to three weeks.
reasons.environment: High specificity limits non-target harm, but field propagation and resistance are untested.

reasons.reproducibility: Pilot-scale reactors with enriched bacterial consortia on carriers need a sponsor lab.
reasons.effectiveness: Algicidal ratio 87.69%, but 36.47% of inhibition was due to filler shading, not bacteria.
reasons.environment: Released DOM and disinfection by-product precursors were measured.

reasons.reproducibility: Bench flask assays, but needs a purchased marine dinoflagellate culture and purified prodigiosin.
reasons.effectiveness: Triplicate flasks: >=0.08 ug/mL killed 97% by 48 h with no recovery, though 0.03-0.05 ug/mL let cells regrow by 72 h; one species only.
reasons.cost: Purified prodigiosin and a purchased P. donghaiense culture run roughly $150-500.
reasons.time: Kill was >80% at 24 h and 97% at 48 h.
reasons.environment: The algicidal 0.1 ug/mL dose killed 49% of Artemia and 20% of juvenile sea bass in 24 h; the safety margin is only ~1.2x.

reasons.reproducibility: Flask co-culture is bench-scale but needs a purchased Microcystis strain and T. versicolor culture with sterile technique.
reasons.effectiveness: About 85% of M. aeruginosa removed in 30 h, but one strain at flask scale with two biological replicates and efficacy not the main aim.
reasons.cost: Purchased fungal and algal cultures plus media cost about $150-500.
reasons.time: Chl a fell to one sixth of initial within 30 h.
reasons.environment: Live fungus added; non-target and environmental effects were not assessed.
